parsed.explanation: The division itself is genuinely protective: a public-accommodations law covering gender identity since 2008, protected all-gender facility access, working hate-crime enforcement (including a bias murder conviction), an abolished gay-panic defence, care-shield and safe-passage law, a custody consent decree with specialised housing and payment, and courts that enforced anti-discrimination against a hospital. Those mitigate in-state exposure to roughly the reduced-risk tier. But the shared parent regime is the operative hardest rule and is traveller-facing: sex-assigned-at-birth passport/visa markers, refusal where documents cast doubt, possible lifetime fraud ineligibility, an entry ban on trans athletes, federal-building facility bans, invasive screening, and documented beatings, forced labour and sexual abuse in immigration custody. State law cannot displace border, federal-facility or immigration-detention practice, so the division sits only moderately above the parent line — elevated, not reduced, risk.
